blocks.text: AppArmor confines application and system helper access. Endpoint Security → AppArmor provides status, events and deliberately authorized policy operations. Enforce mode denies disallowed operations; complain mode records events and has a different security meaning.

Profiles are installed in /etc/apparmor.d/ and the managed mode policy is separate. Local includes supplement specific profiles. A source profile existing on disk does not prove it is loaded, attached to the application or enforcing.

Record the time, exact application/menu action and the sanitized denial details through the existing status/events tools. Include which profile and requested operation were involved. Investigate the required narrow permission before authorizing any change.
Do not disable AppArmor globally, unload profiles or broadly allow execution to make an application launch. Help never changes policy, modes, cache or kernel security state.
